auth_flow: 1. Create an API Key in My CJ (Apps > install "API" app > https://www.cjdropshipping.com/my.html#/authorize/API > Add API, Type=API Key, copy key). Installing the app alone does not create a key.
2. POST /authentication/getAccessToken with body {"apiKey": "<CJ API key>"} -> data.openId, accessToken, accessTokenExpiryDate, refreshToken, refreshTokenExpiryDate, createDate.
3. Cache tokens server-side only (never send to front end). Send header CJ-Access-Token on every call.
4. On code 1600001 (invalid/expired token) call POST /authentication/refreshAccessToken {"refreshToken": ...}; if that returns 1600003 (invalid refresh token) call getAccessToken again.
5. POST /authentication/logout invalidates the access token (after logout a new token is generated on next getAccessToken).

Token caching: multiple getAccessToken calls by the same account within 24 hours return the same accessToken/refreshToken (server-side cache); refreshAccessToken also returns the cached token within the 24h window. After 24h or after explicit logout a new token is generated.
getAccessToken is rate limited like other endpoints: max 1 call/second (QPS=1) per the Auth page.
openId (from getAccessToken) is also the HMAC secret for webhook signature verification - keep it secret.

MCP: CJ also runs an MCP server (local stdio build from github.com/CJ-dropshipping/api-mcp, or remote https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/mcp/<MCP_TOKEN>); its local mode logs in with CJ email + password (verify_credentials tool). Separate from the REST API key flow.

token_lifetimes.cache_window: Same token returned for repeated getAccessToken/refreshAccessToken within 24 hours
token_lifetimes.reauthorization: If both are expired obtain new tokens via getAccessToken with the API key

rate_limits.per_ip: No more than 10 requests/second per IP address; each IP limited to 3 users ("one ip limit 3 users, Your Ip is XXX").
endpoint_specific: Listing publishAsync/publishSync/republish: max 2 requests/second per account
Get Shop List and Create Product Connection have their own "Rate Limit" notes (see endpoint rate_limit)
Query Products By Image: requires account Level 3+ (below gets 401), 1000 points per call
Legacy (pre-points) /product/list note: free or v1 users max 1000 requests/day (2024-09-30); one IP max three users
Dispute uploadFile: 10MB per file, daily upload limit (error 1607020, resets next day Beijing time)
rate_limits.exceeded: HTTP 429 with code 1600200 "Too much request"; 1600201 "Quota has been used up".
raw_text: ## Access Frequency Restrictions
Once you got the access token, your application can successfully call the various interfaces provided by the CJ backend to manage or access the resources of the CJ backend.

In order to prevent application errors from causing an abnormal load on the CJ server, by default, each CJ user is limited to a certain rate of interface calls, and when this limit is exceeded, the corresponding interface call will receive a error code.
The following is the current default frequency limit, which may be adjusted by the CJ backend depending on operational conditions.
## Base Frequency
- No more than 10 requests/second per IP address;
- The maximum call frequency for non-login interfaces is 30 requests/second.
- Each IP address is limited to 3 users. When this limit is exceeded, the response will be: `one ip limit 3 users, Your Ip is XXX`.
## Special Frequency
Special settings:
- The interface restricts user access frequency based on user level:
- For Free users or the sales level is 0 or 1, it is limited to 1 request/second;
- For Plus users or the sales level is 2, it is limited to 2 requests/second;
- For Prime users or the sales level is 3, it is limited to 4 requests/second;
- For Advanced users or the sales level is 4 or 5, it is limited to 6 requests/second.
Referer CJ Prime  (opens new window)
## Daily Available Points
Notice

The previous "Daily Call Limit" mechanisms have been deprecated. CJ now uses a points-based daily quota system. Please refer to the new API Points Resource Rules documentation for full details on how your daily API usage is calculated and how to increase your quota.
←  Sandbox   Points Resource Rules  →

quotas.model: Points-based daily quota replaced "daily call count" model. Effective June 1, 2026 for users registered on/after June 1 2026; July 1, 2026 for earlier users. Until then old QPS + daily call limits applied.
quotas.daily_points: Total = Base 50,000 points/day (reset 00:00 UTC) + Order Conversion (MAX of last 3 months transaction amount x 100 points per USD, recalculated daily). Base deducted first.
quotas.replenishment: Per-minute replenishment = Total/1440; available never exceeds daily Total; pointsInfo.remaining never negative.
quotas.insufficient: HTTP 429 code 429 "Insufficient API points..." with pointsInfo; global error table also lists 16900500 "Insufficient points".
quotas.points_vs_money: Points are an API quota, not money; they are not purchased directly. Quota grows with order spend (100 points per $1 of max monthly transaction amount over the last 3 months). Endpoints not in the table cost 0 points.
quotas.suspension: Zero transaction amount for 30 consecutive days -> API access suspended (reminder email after 7 days). Every call then returns 1600014 until reactivated on the My CJ API page.
quotas.listing_billing: All /listed/* endpoints (30) cost 10 points per call, billed even on failure; poll queryPublishStatus at >= 5 s intervals.
quotas.settings_quota_fields: Get Settings returns setting.quotaLimits[] {quotaUrl, quotaLimit, quotaType (0-total,1-per year,2-per year(sic),3-per quarter,4-per day,5-per hour)} and qpsLimit.

webhooks.registration: POST /webhook/set with topic objects product, stock, order, logistics, makeup, privateOrder, dispute, wallet; each {type: ENABLE|CANCEL, callbackUrls: [one public HTTPS URL]}.
webhooks.requirements: HTTPS (TLS1.2/1.3), POST, Content-Type application/json, respond HTTP 200 within 3 seconds; no localhost/127.0.0.1.
webhooks.signature: Header `sign` = Base64(HMAC-SHA256(key=str(openId), message=raw request body)). Compare as strings; do not re-serialize body.
webhooks.retries: No retry: a message that does not get 200 OK (or times out) is not resent. Sustained failures trigger auto-close; re-register to resume. Reconcile with query APIs.
webhooks.product_subscription: Product/variant/stock pushes filtered by product subscription (/webhook/product/subscribe). After July 2026 subscribeAll=true no longer available; must subscribe specific product IDs.
webhooks.delayed_merge: Product/variant ~2 min merge window; stock/logistics ~5 min.
notable_gaps: Sell-price-only variant changes are not pushed
Regular orders are not pushed on creation (only private inventory outbound orders push INSERT)

api_page_prose: - Encryption: TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 recommended for secure transmission
- Timeout: Response must be returned within 3 seconds  (Avoid long-running or complex business logic to ensure prompt response)
- URL Validation: The callback URL must be a public `HTTPS` address. Local addresses such as `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are not supported.
- Failure Message: If URL validation fails, the `message` field will return the concrete reason directly.
Dispute messages cover less than the dispute query endpoints
Dispute messages are only pushed for disputes on orders that can be resolved to a store, whereas Query dispute messages / Reply dispute cover all disputes under your account.

As a result you may find a dispute that the API can read and reply to, but never delivers a webhook for. That is expected behaviour, not a delivery failure. Do not treat webhooks as a complete list of your disputes — reconcile periodically against the dispute list endpoint.

Also note that a new reply from CJ support does not trigger this message — it is only pushed when the dispute status changes. To detect "the other side replied", use the `updateDate` field returned by the dispute list endpoint.
Subscribe specific products or enable subscribe-all mode for product/variant/stock webhook notifications.
Note: Subscribing specific products and subscribing all products are mutually exclusive.
- If `productIds` is provided, only the specified products will be subscribed, and subscribe-all will be automatically disabled.
- If only `subscribeAll=true` is provided (without `productIds`), all previously subscribed specific products will be cleared.
- Before July 2026, only users registered before June 2026 may subscribe to all products(`subscribeAll=true`)
- After July 2026, `subscribeAll=true` will no longer be available for any user; you must specify product IDs to subscribe
Remove specific products from the subscription list.
Query the list of subscribed products with pagination support.
When a product or variant changes, the webhook notification is sent based on user's subscription:
- If user has `subscribeAllProducts=true` → notification is sent
- If user has subscribed the specific product → notification is sent
Stock change notifications follow the same product subscription filtering rules. Only users who subscribed the corresponding product will receive stock change notifications.
- Webhook success/failure counts are recorded per hour per topic
- If the success rate in each of the previous 2 complete hours is below 80% (configurable), the webhook topic will be automatically closed
- Close reason is recorded in the system
Private inventory outbound orders reuse the Order message (ORDER) topic; once the order webhook is enabled you receive them without a separate subscription:
- A `messageType=INSERT` message is pushed when the private inventory outbound order is created (regular orders are not pushed on INSERT);
- Subsequent status/payment/shipment changes are pushed as `UPDATE`, same as regular orders;
- The order message `params` carries `privateOutboundOrder=true` for these orders, `false` for regular orders;
- For the order message body fields, see Start - Webhook Order message.
The tables below list when you will receive a push for each topic. Changes that are not listed (internal fields, version columns, statistics columns, etc.) do not trigger a push.

Product, variant, stock and logistics use delayed merged delivery: multiple changes to the same record inside a merge window are combined into a single message instead of one message per change. The current window is about 2 minutes for product/variant and about 5 minutes for stock/logistics (a server-side tuning parameter that may change — do not rely on its exact value). Order, makeup bill, private order and wallet are pushed in real time.

- "Key product fields" are: category, product name (CN/EN), SKU, main image, sell price, description, listing status, property 1/2/3, English property, supplier, product type, product visibility. Only these fields trigger a push; `params.fields` lists the field names that changed within the merge window.
- "Key variant fields" are: variant English name, length, width, height, weight, image, sell price, spec value 1/2/3.

- A variant change that only affects the sell price is currently not pushed (when no other key field changes together with the price); product-side platform-wide repricing campaigns are not pushed either. Use the query APIs as the source of truth for price.
- A physical row deletion produces no push. `DELETE` means "this product/variant is no longer sellable to you", not that the record was deleted.
- Product subscription filtering (see 3.1) is applied before the push.
- Only changes to variant, product, warehouse, available quantity and actual quantity trigger a push.

- `messageType` only indicates the source event (insert/update vs delete); it does not indicate the direction of the stock change. Use `storageNum` per warehouse in the payload as the authoritative quantity.
- Product subscription filtering (see 3.2) is applied before the push.
- Regular orders are not pushed on creation; only private inventory outbound orders push `INSERT` (see 3.4).
- Precondition: order number, logistics status and tracking number must all have a value; otherwise nothing is pushed.
- A change of the internal version column alone is not pushed.
The trigger points for these three topics are described in "4 Makeup Bill Message", "5 Private Order Message (PrivateOrder)" and "6 Wallet Notifications" below.
After subscribing, the following makeup-bill changes are pushed to the registered `makeup` callback URL:

Order number notes: `orderId` is the makeup bill number, always `BT`-prefixed (e.g. `BT2606061320024499900`), same as `orderCode` in the makeup list; `relationOrderId` is the original CJ order being made up — its type depends on the original order (private inventory outbound `SD…`, dropshipping/direct, etc.) and can be used to look up the original order via the order query API.

The request carries a `sign` header: `sign = Base64( HmacSHA256( secret = your openId string, message = raw JSON request body ) )`. Compute HmacSHA256 over the raw body with your openId as the secret, Base64-encode it, and compare with the `sign` header.
Same as other topics: return `200 OK` within 3 seconds; failed pushes are not retried (messages are not resent); continuous failures trigger the auto-close mechanism (see 3.3).

After subscribing the `privateOrder` topic, status changes of private orders (SY order / private inventory order, order number prefixed with `SY`) are pushed to the registered callback URL. Only SY orders are pushed (dropshipping/deposit orders are excluded).

Same as other topics: `sign = Base64( HmacSHA256( secret = your openId string, message = raw JSON request body ) )`; return `200 OK` within 3 seconds; failed pushes are not retried (messages are not resent); continuous failures trigger the auto-close mechanism (see 3.3).

After you subscribe to the `wallet` topic, a notification is pushed to your registered `wallet` callback URL whenever a new billing record is created in your CJ wallet, or the amount or status of an existing record changes. The data comes from the same billing record table as My CJ → Wallet → Billing History, but notifications do not apply the page's type filtering or status mapping, so you may receive more records than the page shows (see 6.5).

- Add a `wallet` object to the "1.1 Message Setting" request body, in the same format as other topics (`type` + `callbackUrls`). `type` = `ENABLE` turns it on and `CANCEL` turns it off (case-insensitive); an unrecognized value is treated as cancel.

- A wallet subscription belongs to the API account (openId) of the token you use, and can only be set with that account's own token. When the request contains `wallet`, the platform first checks that wallet notifications are available and that the token belongs to that account; if this check fails, the whole request fails and the other topics in the same request are not saved either. The errors are `Wallet notifications are not enabled`, `Authenticated account is required` and `Wallet account ownership mismatch`.

- `wallet` is processed after the other topics in the same request: if the wallet part fails (`callbackUrls` is an empty array or contains only empty strings, the URL is invalid, or the URL test fails), the topics before it in the same request have already been saved; but if `wallet` has no `callbackUrls`, or its `type` is empty or longer than 20 characters, the whole request fails at parameter validation and nothing is saved.

- When you enable or cancel it, the platform first sends a test message to your callback URL to check that it is reachable. It must return `200 OK` within 3 seconds, otherwise the setting fails — so include the callback URL when cancelling too. The test message has `messageId` = `wallet-registration-check`, `type` = `WALLET`, `messageType` = `CREATED`, an `openId` at the top level, and only three fields in `params`: `id` (always `test`), `currency` and `amount` (`0`). It is not a real transaction: recognize it by `messageId`, return `200` and do not book it.
- A successful setting takes effect within about 10 seconds.

- If you have several API accounts, every account that has enabled the wallet subscription receives its own copy: same `messageId`, each signed with that account's openId. Real notifications do not contain the openId in the body, so if several accounts share one callback URL you cannot tell from the body which account a message belongs to. We recommend using a different callback URL for each account.

Fields in `params` that have no value (`null`) are omitted entirely; parse them as optional. Some records do not carry balances (e.g. payments made directly with PayPal, a bank card or other third-party channels, and refunds returned to them); `balanceBefore` and `balanceAfter` are then omitted. Do not calculate the balance by adding up the messages you receive — a message may be delivered more than once, or be missing if your callback failed. Messages are not guaranteed to arrive in order: the `CREATED` and `UPDATED` of one record may arrive in reverse order. Overwrite by `params.id` and keep the one with the later `eventTime`; for several changes within the same second, check the status and amount with "Query Billing History"; the API converts balances for records with a display currency and does not return internal types `10`–`16` (see 6.5).
When the payment method is system refund, Billing History shows the type name as System Refund, so `params.type` alone cannot fully restore the type name shown on the page.

- Same as other topics: `sign = Base64( HmacSHA256( secret = your openId string, message = raw JSON request body ) )`. Use the openId you received when you obtained the token for that API account (the body does not contain it).
- Return `200 OK` within 3 seconds; only `200` counts as success. Failed pushes are not retried (messages are not resent); continuous failures trigger the auto-close mechanism (see 3.3).
- The same message may be delivered more than once (same `messageId`). Deduplicate by `messageId` and make your processing idempotent.
To fill gaps, pull records by time range with the "Query Billing History" API. Records can be matched by `id`, but the two differ in these ways:
- The API does not return internal types `10`–`16`, and shows statuses `5` and `6` as `0`;
- The API does not return the fee or the balance before the transaction, so these two cannot be filled from it;
- If the record carries a display currency, the API converts balances to that currency; notifications carry the original USD values;

- For payments linked to an original order (such as makeup payments), the API returns the original order number as `cjOrderId`, while the notification's `orderId` is the number recorded on the billing record;
- The API filters by record creation date; to catch later status changes of an older record, query by its creation date.

endpoints.name: Get access token
endpoints.description: Token-based authentication, the life of an access-token is 180 days, and the life of a refresh-token is 180 days. You can obtain new a access-tokens with refresh-token when access-token expired. You need to obtain a new access-token when refresh-token expired. Rate limit is consistent with other API endpoints: maximum 1 call per second (QPS = 1). Token Caching: When the same account calls the Get Token endpoint multiple times within 24 hours, the returned accessToken and refreshToken remain consistent (server-side cache). The Refresh Token endpoint also returns the same cached token within the 24-hour window. After 24 hours or after an explicit logout, a new token will be generated.

endpoints.name: Query API Call Logs
endpoints.description: Returns the calls your account made to this open platform, newest first: which endpoint, when, the HTTP status, how long it took and, for failed calls, the error code and message. Use it to investigate failures by `requestId` or to find out why you were throttled (`1600200`). 20 points per call. Rate limit: the per-user QPS of your account level applies (1–6 requests/second, see Access Frequency Restrictions); exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with code `1600200`. Calls rejected before reaching the endpoint — rate limited, insufficient points, account frozen — are recorded too. Calls with an invalid or expired access token cannot be attributed to an account and do not appear. Logs are written asynchronously, so a call may take a short while to show up. For security, request parameters, request headers, response bodies and client IPs are never returned.

endpoints.name: Query Packaging Products (with Inventory)
endpoints.description: Page through the packaging products available to the current customer, at the variant dimension (B-side "pick a packaging" scenario). Dimension note (key difference from 1.9): this endpoint is at the variant dimension — `content[].id` is the variant ID (vid) and can be passed directly as `packVid` when creating a packaging connection; each row also carries "variant SKU / dimensions (L×W×H) / inventory / connected count", for picking a packaging variant and building a connection; `packingKey` is matched as a whole combination (exact); marketing search bans and site risk control are not applied. 1.9 is at the product dimension — its `id` is the product ID (pid) and it only exposes "image / name / price (range price)", matches `packingKey` key-by-key, and does apply marketing search bans and site risk control. ⚠️ Both endpoints return a field named `id`, but they mean different things: 1.8's `id` = variant ID (vid), 1.9's `id` = product ID (pid). Only the endpoint tells them apart — the field name does not. `packVid` for a packaging connection must come from 1.8's `id`; passing 1.9's `id` will not link. Note · implementation granularity (paging and row count are per product): downstream pages by packaging product — one product yields one row, and that row's `id` / `sku` / L/W/H are taken from the product's first variant. So this endpoint cannot enumerate all variants of a packaging product, and `totalRecords` is a product count, not a variant count. Note · two different granularities within the same row: `goodNum` (inventory) is aggregated per product — the total across all variants and all warehouses of that product; `correlationNum` (connected count) is counted for that row's variant only. Do not compare them as if they were the same granularity.

endpoints.notes: Creates a customised (POD/individualization) product in CJ. https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/product/individualization/add Below is a complete, actually working request (four colour variants, one text design area). Replace the values with those of your own product: Three things in this example are the ones most often got wrong: - `img` is a single string with multiple URLs joined by commas (four variant renders in the example) — it is not an array; `bigImg` holds exactly one URL. - `variantKey` and `variants[].variantKey` share a name but not a meaning: the top-level one is the attribute dimension name (`颜色-像素` in the example, dimensions joined by `-`), while the one inside a variant is that variant's attribute values (`Antique Silver-4k`). - `customeDesign` is an array (one element per design area), not a single object — see "customeDesign structure" below. ## Request Parameters About "required": none of the fields above is enforced at the request layer (hence N everywhere), but business-wise `originalPid` / `cid` / `nameEn` / `variants` / `customeDesign` are all indispensable — the CURL above is the minimum working set; send the fields it sends. ## Automatic image transfer URLs sent in `img` / `bigImg` / `variants[].img` are automatically downloaded and transferred to CJ's image storage when they are not already on a CJ image domain; the CJ URL is what gets stored downstream. This avoids product images depending on external links, which may expire, be blocked by hotlink protection, or be unreachable in some regions. - URLs that are already CJ image links are not transferred again and are kept as-is. - A failed transfer does not block product creation: that image keeps the URL you sent and the product is still created. So if a product image is still your own external link, the transfer for that image failed (usually because the URL is not publicly reachable) — send a publicly accessible URL and retry. - The transfer uses `originalPid` to build the storage path, so no transfer happens when `originalPid` is omitted; images are stored with the original URLs. ## Sending multiple images Only `img` accepts multiple images, joined by commas: - `bigImg` and `variants[].img` accept exactly one URL; the whole string is treated as one address, so a comma inside them (URLs may legitimately contain commas) is never used to split the value. - When `img` carries multiple URLs, each of them is evaluated for transfer independently and the value is returned as a comma-joined string. ## customeDesign structure `customeDesign` is an array; each element is one design area on the product (front, back, ...). The structure is produced by the CJ design tool and this endpoint passes it through as-is into the product's customisation data, so field names and casing must be copied exactly (note it is `imgsrc`, not `imgSrc`). Each `layer` element (a text layer in the example): Image layers additionally carry `top` / `left` (position) and fields like `imgScalex`; these are passed through as-is too — send whatever the design tool produced. success failure (duplicate SKU as an example) Important - how to tell whether creation succeeded Rely on `data.statusCode`: `200` means the product was created, and `data.data` is then the SKU of the new customized product. `808` (duplicate SKU) and `504` (creation failed) both mean the product was not created, and the outer `result` will be `false`. Note that on success `data.message` is `"200"` rather than readable text (existing upstream behaviour) - do not use it to determine the result. The creator is recorded by CJ from your API credential automatically - it cannot (and need not) be specified in the request.

endpoints.name: Query Cross-Country Size Chart
endpoints.description: Query the cross-country size chart configured for a product by product id. Returns structured sizing data (the size code for each destination country/region and the measurement value for each size parameter), ready to render a size chart. Note 1.10 Query Product Detail returns the raw stored string of the size chart — its format is not published and parsing it is not recommended. This API returns an already-parsed structured object and is the recommended way. This API supports pid only — `productSku` / `variantSku` are not accepted. If you only have a SKU, first call 1.5 Product Details (which accepts `pid` / `productSku` / `variantSku`), take the `pid` from its response, then call this API. Coverage This capability only covers products created after this feature went live that have a size chart configured. Size charts of older products were not archived in the new way, so this API cannot retrieve them and returns `configured = false`. If you need the size chart of an older product, report the product to your Account Manager (AM); once the AM has filled it in, the product becomes retrievable through this API. This API does not return size chart images. Size chart images are currently embedded in the product description rich text as ordinary images, with no dedicated type marker, so they cannot be reliably distinguished from the description.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/product/sizeChart/query ## Request Parameters Size chart configured Product queryable but no size chart configured Product not found or not queryable Parameters chartData array element chartData[].areaValues array element chartData[].paramValues array element ## Unit reference The weight dimension is the recommended body weight (which weight range this size fits), not the product's net weight. If new dimensions are added later, only a new unitCode value appears — the response structure stays the same and your parsing logic needs no change. ## The four forms of main and sub main and sub are always strings, with four forms that are independent of the dimension (a length can be a range; a weight can be a single value): Do not call parseFloat on main / sub `parseFloat("88-92")` silently truncates to 88 — the upper bound is lost with no error, and your buyer ends up seeing the wrong measurement. Treat them as strings; when you need to tell a single value from a range or an open range, check the ≥ / ≤ prefix and the hyphen yourself. ≥(U+2265) and ≤(U+2264) are non-ASCII characters — make sure your client handles UTF-8. ## Error Codes ## FAQ Why is chartData not ordered from the smallest size to the largest? This API returns the stored order (the same order shown on the CJ product page); it does not represent size order. In the example above the order is L, M, S, XL. Sort it yourself if you need to display sizes from small to large. What is "EU US" in countries? Why is it not a standard country code? It is a combined value meaning "EU/US common sizing". The field is free text and its value is decided when the product is created, so it is not guaranteed to be an ISO country code. Do not parse or match it as a country code. Is "Lenght" in sizeParams a typo? Can I hard-code parameter name matching? Parameter names are the values entered when the product was created; they may contain spelling variants (such as Lenght) or spaces (such as Top Lenght). Do not hard-code parameter name matching — index into paramValues by the order of sizeParams. Does configured = false always mean the product has no size chart? No. Besides "genuinely not configured", a small number of products — supplier products in particular — may also return `configured = false` because of how product data is retrieved upstream. If you can see a size chart for the product on the CJ product page but this API returns false, contact your Account Manager (AM) to verify. How long after configuring a size chart can it be queried through this API? Sizing data comes from a product data snapshot, so there is a short delay after a size chart is configured or modified before it takes effect here. Product visibility is judged from the same snapshot; right after a product is removed from shelves or private-visible authorisation changes, this API may briefly still return the old conclusion — treat 1.5 Product Details as authoritative.

endpoints.name: Create Order V2
endpoints.description: - Create order - `payType=1` or omitted: page payment (default), and `cjPayUrl` will be returned (deprecated, see the notice below) - `payType=2`: balance payment, and the order will continue through add-to-cart, order confirmation, and balance deduction - `payType=3`: create the order only without initiating payment, add-to-cart, or order confirmation - Add param platformToken to header, The way to obtain platformToken is the same as the way to obtain CJ Access Token. If not required, the value can be empty. (2025-01-08 update) cjPayUrl is deprecated The `cjPayUrl` payment page redirect address returned with `payType=1` (page payment) is deprecated and is no longer maintained. Do not use it in new integrations. Please pay in one of the following ways instead: - `payType=2`: pay with balance directly while creating the order; - `payType=3`: create the order only, then call "2.3 Pay Balance V2（POST）" yourself to complete the payment. The field is still returned for backward compatibility with existing integrations, but it is no longer maintained and may stop working or be removed in the future.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/shopping/order/getOrderDetailBatch Notes: the response may contain fewer items than requested — ids that cannot be found or do not belong to your account are silently skipped, so match by `cjOrderCode`; the response is identical to "1.7 Query Order" (since 2026-08-19 the two endpoints return the same response object and the `orderStatus` basis is unified as well, so you can reuse one deserialization model); the only value difference is that `features` is not supported, so `logisticsTimeliness` is always `null` (use the single-order endpoint for logistics timeliness); platform order ids as a query condition and archived orders are not supported (use the single-order endpoint; note the `platformOrderId` field is still returned in the response — "not supported" refers to using it as a lookup key); an internal retrieval failure returns `code=1600000` (never `200` with an empty array — retry later); rate limit 2 requests/second/account. Change on 2026-08-19 (two parts — part 1 is backward compatible, part 2 is a value change): - 8 previously omitted fields are now returned: `trackingUrl`, `trackingProvider`, `isSandbox`, `platformOrderId` at order level and `lineItemId`, `storeLineItemId`, `productionOrderStatus`, `abnormalType` at product level (even though the text above already claimed the structure matched). The value semantics of `trackingUrl` and the carrier-name mapping are aligned with the single-order endpoint too (previously this endpoint's `trackingUrl` was always `null`). This part is additive only — no existing field name or meaning changed, so no action is needed for current integrations. - The `orderStatus` basis now matches "1.7": this endpoint previously returned codes 300–399 directly as `PENDING` and 400–499 as `PROCESSING`; it now always returns the aggregate `UNSHIPPED`, refined by `subStatus=PENDING/PROCESSING` (same as "1.7"). If you previously detected unshipped orders on this endpoint via `orderStatus=PENDING`/`PROCESSING`, switch to `orderStatus=UNSHIPPED` + `subStatus`. "1.7 Query Order" itself is unchanged. success `data` is an array; each element has exactly the same fields as the object returned by `1.7 Query Order`. The example below contains two orders: the first one has shipped (so it has a tracking number and a tracking URL), the second has not shipped yet (so `trackNumber` / `trackingProvider` / `trackingUrl` are empty). The four optional fee fields below use USD and two decimal places with HALF_UP rounding. Null or omitted means unavailable; explicit zero means a recorded zero. For applicable IOSS orders, tax plus its handling fee gives the IOSS total; where the rate is 3%, line-level rounding can differ from rounding the order-level VAT total multiplied by 3%. endpoints.name: Query Order Logs
endpoints.description: Returns the log of one order — the same records you see under Order Logs in My CJ. Free (no points). Rate limit: the per-user QPS of your account level applies (1–6 requests/second, see Access Frequency Restrictions); exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with code `1600200`. Two modes: - Default (`fullTimeline` omitted or `false`): only the Dispatched record(s). This is the original behaviour of this endpoint and is unchanged. - Full timeline (`fullTimeline=true`): all log records of the order returned by the log service, newest first, each with the stage it belongs to (`nodeName`). Only your own orders can be queried: an order that does not exist and an order that belongs to another account both return `1603100`, in both modes. Change for existing callers (2026-10): before this change the default mode returned the Dispatched record without checking that the order is yours. Orders of other accounts now return `1603100`; the output for your own orders is unchanged. If ownership cannot be verified because the order service is unavailable, the call returns `1600000` (retry later). An order archived long ago is restored automatically on first query; in the rare case the restore fails it returns `1603100`.

endpoints.notes: URL: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/shopping/privateInventory/outbound/progress Lock-failure handling: when `createStatus=LOCK_FAIL`, `nextAction=ADJUST_LOCK_FAIL_PRODUCTS`, or `lockFails` is not empty, do not call `/submit` directly and do not keep relying on `create.submit=true` auto-submit. First call `/detail` to get the current outbound order and product-line echo data. Then delete failed product lines or reduce `productList[].quantity` according to `lockFails[].lockQuantity` / `availableQuantity`, call `/create` again with `orderId` to update the outbound order, and continue polling `/progress` until `createProgress=100`, `createStatus=TASK_COMPLETE`, `lockFails` is empty, and `nextAction=SUBMIT_ORDER`. Partial lock success does not mean the whole order can be submitted; submit only after every updated product line can be locked.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/logistic/unavailableShippingMethods ## Request The request body is identical to 1.2 Freight Calculation Tip — same fields, same types, same meaning. The full parameter table is repeated here so that you can stay on this page while building the request. Four of these fields are validated before the request is sent downstream. If any of them is missing, the whole request fails with `1600300` and the message names the offending row, for example `reqDTOS[0].weight must be greater than 0`. The same four checks also apply to 1.2, so an invalid payload returns the same error code and the same message on both endpoints. success The two lists are complementary: the same `optionName` never appears in both. ## Reason codes (`unavailableList.errorCode`) `unavailableList` does not necessarily list every excluded shipping method. Reasons that are only meaningful internally (route or channel configuration) are filtered out before the response is built, so this list may be shorter than the number of shipping methods actually excluded by the trial calculation. A shipping method missing from both lists was excluded for such an internal reason — contact your CJ agent with the `requestId` if you need to know why. New reason codes may be added over time. Treat an unknown `errorCode` as "unavailable for a reason described in `errorEn`" rather than failing. error

endpoints.name: Available Shipping Methods by SKU
endpoints.description: Lists the shipping methods available for one SKU shipped from a given country — the same list as the shipping method picker in My CJ (product / connection pages). Exclusive shipping methods configured for your account are included. 10 points per call. Rate limit: the per-user QPS of your account level applies (1–6 requests/second, see Access Frequency Restrictions); exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with code `1600200`. Use it before 1.5 Reachable Countries: 1.4 gives you `logisticsName`, 1.5 tells you which countries that shipping method can reach. Unlike 1.1 Freight Calculation, this endpoint does not need a destination country, weight or volume and does not return prices; use 1.1 / 1.2 once you know the destination. Call order: Product Details (get `productSku` or `variants[].variantSku`) → Global Warehouse List (get the shipping-from `countryCode`) → 1.4 → 1.5.

endpoints.name: Look Up Replaced Tracking Number
endpoints.description: When a package is re-shipped or its tracking number is replaced, the tracking number your customer has (or that you synced to your store) stops updating. Send that old tracking number here to find out which of your orders it belongs to, what the order's current tracking number is, and the latest tracking event of both numbers — enough to tell your customer what happened and where to follow the new package. 10 points per call. Rate limit: the per-user QPS of your account level applies (1–6 requests/second, see Access Frequency Restrictions); exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with code `1600200`. Call order: old tracking number → this endpoint → `currentTrackNumber` → 2.1 Get Tracking Information for the full tracking events of the current number. You can also send a number that is still current: it is returned as well, with `trackNumber` equal to `currentTrackNumber` (that is how you tell "not replaced"). A number is left out of `data` (no error) when: - CJ cannot find it; - the order it belongs to is not yours; - the order it belongs to is archived, or has been split / merged into other orders — the same orders Query Orders In Batch cannot return. So an empty `data` array means "none of these numbers could be matched to an order of yours", never "the service failed" — a failure always returns an error code.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/disputes/getDisputeList success error ## About updateDate `updateDate` is the last-modified time of the dispute record. Use it to detect that a dispute has moved on (including a new reply from CJ support) without polling each dispute's detail. Do not use updateDate as the only cursor for incremental sync This field is the update time of the dispute record row, not the maximum timestamp across every action in the dispute lifecycle. Records exist whose `updateDate` is earlier than their final processing time, so pulling only `updateDate > lastSyncTime` will miss disputes. Recommended usage: use `updateDate` for change detection, and additionally run a periodic full re-pull by create-date range as a safety net. ## Date and status semantics startDate/endDate filter creation time, not updateDate. Omitted filters retain previous behavior. Use overlapping reconciliation windows and deduplicate by dispute ID because both boundaries are exclusive. V2 status codes: 100=Pending processing, 200=Pending review, 300=Finance review, 400=On hold, 500=Customer confirmation, 510=Supplier refund finance review, 520=Awaiting payment, 530=Payment processing, 540=Arbitration reserved, 600=Completed, 700=Cancelled, 800=Arbitration cancelled. DISPUTE webhook types 1–5 are not these filter codes. updateDate is a nullable millisecond timestamp returned as a string, and remains a change indicator, not a complete incremental cursor. Existing DISPUTE webhooks are unchanged. ## Filtering by last-updated time Pass `updateDateFrom` / `updateDateTo` (UTC milliseconds) to list only disputes whose `updateDate` falls in `[updateDateFrom, updateDateTo)`. Results are sorted by `updateDate` ascending, then by dispute ID. Both values are required together, and the range may not exceed 31 days, measured in UTC milliseconds (a whole calendar month in a local time zone can exceed 31 days when it contains a daylight-saving change). For a historical catch-up over a longer period, request consecutive windows: use the previous window's `updateDateTo` as the next window's `updateDateFrom` (lower bound inclusive, upper bound exclusive, so adjacent windows neither overlap nor skip; for routine incremental syncs, overlap rounds as described below). They can be combined with `startDate` / `endDate` (both conditions apply). An invalid range (only one bound, a negative value, an upper bound not later than the lower bound, more than 31 days, or an upper bound later than 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z) returns HTTP 400 with `code` `1600300` and `message` `updateDateFrom/updateDateTo must be paired UTC milliseconds, updateDateTo later than updateDateFrom, within 31 days`. Use it to detect changes, and keep a periodic full re-pull - `updateDate` has second precision (always a multiple of 1000) and becomes visible only after the change is committed, so set `updateDateTo` to now minus at least 5 minutes. The upper bound must be in the past: with a future upper bound, a dispute updated while you page can stay inside the window and push another one out of your pages without changing `total`. - Keep one window fixed for a whole sync round: with the same `updateDateFrom` / `updateDateTo`, request `pageNum=1, 2, …` until a page returns fewer than `pageSize` rows (or `pageNum × pageSize` ≥ `total`). Do not move the window between pages. - A dispute updated during the round moves out of the window, so later rows shift forward by one and a row you have not read yet can be skipped. If the `total` on the last page differs from the first page, re-run the round from page 1 with the same window; if it keeps changing, use a smaller window (for example one hour). - Make the next round's window overlap the previous one (for example, start 5 minutes before the previous `updateDateTo`) and deduplicate by `disputeId`, keeping the latest. A dispute updated during a round shows up again in a later window with its new `updateDate`. - An unchanged `total` does not prove nothing was skipped (for example, a change that becomes visible later than the 5-minute margin), and disputes whose `updateDate` is empty never match this filter. Some processing steps do not refresh `updateDate` (see "About updateDate" above). Keep the overlap and a periodic full re-pull by creation date.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/disputes/uploadFile One file per request; call it once per attachment. URL requirements - Must be a publicly accessible `http://` / `https://` URL on the default port (80 / 443), without user:password; private-network addresses are rejected. - The URL must still be valid when you call: CJ downloads it synchronously within this call; once stored, the original URL is no longer needed. - Redirects are followed up to 3 times; every redirect target must also be a public address. - The source must start responding within 20 seconds, the whole download must finish within 120 seconds, and it must return HTTP 200. - URLs without a file extension or with signature parameters are fine — CJ detects the type from the file content. File requirements - Images and videos together are limited to 2GB per account per day. Days are counted in Beijing time (UTC+8). - The format is detected from the file content, regardless of the extension in the URL; svg, html and similar content is rejected. - Failed copies do not count toward the daily limits. - Each call costs 20 points (see API points), charged per call, including calls rejected by validation. About the returned URL - The URL is on a CJ domain and is publicly accessible without login: - Images open directly in the browser as a preview, not as a download; - Videos play directly in the browser (mp4 and webm work in all major browsers; whether a mov plays depends on its codec, so prefer mp4). - The URL does not expire; CJ does not delete it automatically, so it stays reachable during and after the dispute. - Anyone with the URL can open it — do not copy files that contain personal data, passwords or other sensitive information. - Put it in `imageUrl` when `fileType` is `IMAGE`, and in `videoUrl` when it is `VIDEO`. success error ## Example: copy first, then create the dispute - Copy the attachment and take `data.url` from the response: - Put `data.url` in `imageUrl` / `videoUrl` of "3 Create dispute" (or "8 Reply dispute"): ← 6 Logistic 8 Webhook →

endpoints.name: Query Product Connection Logs
endpoints.description: Returns the history of connecting / disconnecting your store products to CJ products — the Connection Records you see in My CJ. Use it to find out when and how a store variant got (or lost) its CJ product, e.g. after an order was not matched. 20 points per call. Records are newest first. At least one filter is required (there is no time range filter). Rate limit: the per-user QPS of your account level applies (1–6 requests/second, see Access Frequency Restrictions); exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with code `1600200`. Good to know: - A `shopId` that is not yours is not rejected; it simply matches nothing (records are always limited to your account). - `shopName`, the store / CJ product and variant titles and images, `platformVariantSku` and `cjVariantKey` are read at query time, so they show the current values and are null if the product or variant has since been deleted. `operationType`, `operationTime`, the IDs and `relevanceStatus` are recorded when the operation happened. - An empty page normally means no record matches. In rare cases it can also mean the log service was temporarily unavailable — if you expect records, retry later.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/ticket/create ⚠️ What `requestNo` actually protects (corrected on 2026-09-07 after production testing): It only blocks repeated submissions with the same `requestNo` within 5 seconds (returning `1609006 Duplicate submit`). It is a 5-second lock, not an idempotency key. After 5 seconds, the same `requestNo` will create another ticket. Measured: two submissions 5.7 seconds apart produced two identical tickets. Therefore do not blindly retry after a network timeout. Instead, call `POST /ticket/list` (newest first) to check whether the previous attempt already succeeded, then decide whether to resubmit. `requestNo` only guards against double-clicks and similar bursts. This endpoint does not return a ticketId. To locate the ticket you just created, call Ticket List afterwards and take the newest one.

endpoints.notes: https://developers.cjdropshipping.com/api2.0/v1/listed/publishAsync ## Request parameters Common fields (all platforms): variants fields: Platform-specific fields: Shopee (CNSC stores must be authorized with "Auth Merchant", otherwise 10030) Title, description, image count, variant count etc. must satisfy the limits from `publishProductLimit`; the description must be longer than 20 characters. TikTok / TikTok US / TikTok US Cross Title up to 255 characters (≤188 ASCII characters recommended); at most 9 main images. US stores must bind CJ warehouses in TikTok Shop Seller Center first, otherwise 10060. Price converted to USD must not exceed 100000; at most 256 SKU combinations. At most 100 variants; total variant stock must not exceed the listing type `maxStock`; variant images at least 500×500. Temu / Temu US Local For Temu non-apparel products `images` needs at least 3; variants of the same color must have the same price; variant length ≥ width ≥ height. Temu US Local prices are always USD and `productOptionNameList` has at most 2 names. Whop / Nuvemshop: common fields only. Whop always uses USD, title ≤80 characters, at most 8 images. ## Request example (Shopify) Success Error A non-empty `data` only means CJ has accepted the request; the final result comes from `queryPublishStatus`. ## Error codes (async platforms) In addition to 0.5 common error codes:

All variants of a customized product lack customization details

CJ warehouse not bound in TikTok Shop Seller Center

Temu listing error; the message contains the reason

If the category does not support multi-variation (`singleSkuListing = true` from `getCategoryFeatureList` / `getChildCategoryList`), each variant is listed as a separate listing, at most 10 variants per call; `data` is the URL of the first listing and `message` is `Listed N of M variants.` with failure details. Gateway trace id — Provide it when contacting CJ support

Names involved in the rejection — Fields, tables or functions that caused the rejection, for example `["salesman"]` for `COLUMN_NOT_REGISTERED`. Empty on success
The SQL actually executed — Your SQL after CJ added your data scope, the menu's fixed conditions, the time lower bound and the row limit
Result rows — Keys are the column names in your `SELECT`. Null for 1.2 Explain SQL
Conditions added by CJ — For reference only
Data scope applied — Your own data only
Row limit applied — The result never exceeds this number of rows, even if your `LIMIT` is larger
Where the row limit comes from

endpoints.name: Get Knowledge Base
endpoints.description: Returns the knowledge base of a menu: its tables, the meaning of each field, and the fixed conditions CJ adds. It is written for AI agents to build SQL. Free.

request_params.name: menuCode
request_params.notes: See the menu table above. Letters, digits, `_` and `-` only [length 64]

response_fields.description: Knowledge base version — Changes when the knowledge base changes
Tables of the menu — Schema `dd_cj_order` for order menus

Fields you can select — `table`: the table it belongs to; `exposedName`: the name to use in SQL; `physicalType`: the column type; `virtual`: `true` means CJ computes the value, write `exposedName` directly; `note`: the meaning of the field (in Chinese)
Fixed conditions added by CJ — `renderedExample` shows the condition. You do not need to write them yourself
